articles.title_en: Manchester City’s data team reshapes squad using a 650,000-player database.
articles.title_ru: Данные команды «Манчестер Сити» трансформируют состав, используя базу из 650 000 игроков.
articles.preview_en: Manchester City’s analytics department rebuilt the squad by mining a 650,000-player database.
articles.preview_ru: Отдел аналитики «Манчестер Сити» перестроил состав, используя базу из 650 000 игроков.
articles.full_en: Manchester City’s data scientists sparked a quiet revolution in player recruitment. The club’s analysts examined a database of 650,000 professional players to identify hidden talent. The team has paired statistical models with traditional scouting to overhaul the roster over the past 18 months. This data-driven approach has delivered several high-impact signings, including a versatile midfielder from the Dutch league. Other Premier League clubs are now studying City’s methodology as a blueprint for modern squad building. Supporters witness the results on the pitch as City’s possession-based style becomes more adaptable and resilient. The success of the database strategy proves that numbers can shape football destiny as powerfully as talent.
articles.full_ru: Аналитики «Манчестер Сити» начали тихую революцию в подборе игроков. Специалисты клуба изучили базу из 650 000 профессиональных футболистов, чтобы выявить скрытые таланты. Команда сочетала статистические модели с традиционным скаутингом, полностью изменив состав за последние 18 месяцев. Этот подход привёл к нескольким ключевым трансферам, включая универсального полузащитника из голландской лиги. Другие клубы Премьер-лиги изучают методологию Сити как образец современного формирования состава. Болельщики уже ощущают изменения на поле, где стиль владения мячом стал более гибким и устойчивым. Успех стратегии на основе данных доказывает, что цифры могут формировать футбольную судьбу так же сильно, как талант.

articles.preview_ru: Mima, Middlesbrough In a truly competitive year, Kira Freije’s apocalyptic humanoids trounce everything in their path, even the sculpture that looks like a pile of biscuits The Turner prize is most ex
articles.full_en: Mima, Middlesbrough In a truly competitive year, Kira Freije’s apocalyptic humanoids trounce everything in their path, even the sculpture that looks like a pile of biscuits The Turner prize is most exciting when you passionately support one of the artists and want to convince everyone she’s a genius. In this year’s show at Middlesbrough Institute of Modern Art, I felt that thrill so strongly, I want to get a T-shirt made to support my artist like the Boro scarves and banners you see around here. Kira Freije has her own floor, separated by a tall flight of stairs from the three other shortlisted artists, because apparently the fine watery mist in her installation could damage their fragile materials. Yet setting her apart seems like a statement and it’s justified. She shows 33 lifesize statues of tragicomic steampunk cyborgs, individual works but gathered in a vaporous apocalyptic wasteland, with an impact and resonance that’s on a level of its own.
